blockers.finding: The job cannot read the T03 phase files under the spec's 768 MiB address-space limit. pyarrow with its default memory pool fails (ArrowMemoryError / bad_alloc) inside read_t03_observations, after the output root has been created. Reproduced read-only with ulimit -v 786432 on one record (AB04/i0 phase.parquet, nice 19, ionice idle): default pool fails; ARROW_DEFAULT_MEMORY_POOL=system with pq.read_table still peaks at 773 MB virtual (limit 786 MB, too close); the guarded launcher sets ARROW_NUM_THREADS=1 but not the pool.
blockers.tested_fix: Set ARROW_DEFAULT_MEMORY_POOL=system (os.environ.setdefault at the top of the runner, before any pyarrow import) and read the two columns with ParquetFile(buffer_size=0).iter_batches(batch_size=4096, columns=[...], use_threads=False). Measured after numpy, h5py and the runner import: VmPeak 347 MB, RSS 101 MiB, 165 observation ids for AB04/i0. The write path (write_observation_table plus reload_check, 250 observations x 20 channels) peaked at 651 MB virtual under the same limit, so it fits but with less headroom; the real run adds the hook and h5py data on top.
blockers.consequence_if_launched: Fails closed (non-zero exit, no data harmed) but leaves a non-empty new output root and burns a spec version. Not a safety issue, a waste.
blockers.required: Fix, rerun tests, regenerate both specs as v2 (the runner hash is bound, so v1 specs become invalid), dry run again. Add a test or a recorded probe that runs read_t03_observations and write_observation_table under RLIMIT_AS 768 MiB.

check_3_mapping_rule.reasoning: Exact id equality is correct and the strictest available. The id embeds dataset, subject, condition, leg and the 1-based source frames a:b, so ids cannot collide across recordings or legs; the runner also refuses an id from another recording, a reference_side that disagrees with the id leg, a duplicate id, and an unparseable id (whole record fails closed). check_3_mapping_rule.residual_risk: Equality of id strings proves the same frame numbers, not that T03 sampled the same window the same way (inclusive 1-based a..b, 150-point linear resample). Nothing in the runner compares signed values with T03's own columns.

Map logical names to the canonical T03 column names and make the pelvis column's leg provenance explicit (pelvis multiplier is settled per leg; the T03 pelvis column is shared).

power_physics.single_leg_hip_power: -1 on the left leg is physically consistent. round_post_b.r01_rule_recommendation: Publish a channel for a recording only if the hook published it for BOTH legs with the same multiplier; if held on either leg, hold it for the whole recording (all-or-nothing per recording and channel), and log which leg decided. Rationale: the release unit is the recording and its column; one-leg publication would give inconsistent coverage between legs and let a half-evidenced channel appear in the release; storage layout and sign are properties of the recording, so a leg-level split is not scientifically meaningful. Do not extend the left multiplier to the right leg by arithmetic: that is a scientific judgment and needs the hook or a reviewed path (it could recover data for AB03/i0, ankle_power in some records). Keep the per-leg hook logs as evidence. Different multipliers on the two legs for the same channel and recording should hold both and be flagged. This matches what the runner does today.

q01_coarse_limits.verdict: Adequate as a blatant-error screen; approve with the edits below. Not a plausibility range.
q01_coarse_limits.textbook_values: Checked via web search: a 2020 supplementary table of AAOS normal ranges lists hip extension 20 and flexion 120, knee flexion 135, ankle plantarflexion 50 and dorsiflexion 20 degrees (https://cdn-links.lww.com/permalink/prsgo/b/prsgo_8_6_2020_04_17_hendriks_gox-d-20-00155r2_sdc1.pdf; also https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9936331/table/TAB2). Another secondary chart gave hip flexion 125 and knee 130, so sources differ by about 5 degrees, irrelevant against a 30 degree margin. I did not reach Norkin and White or the AAOS book themselves: cite AAOS as read through that table, or have José check the book. Widened bounds follow arithmetically: hip -50 to +150 (-20..120 widened), knee -30 to +165 (0..135), ankle -80 to +50 (-50..20 in rule-B dorsiflexion-positive); consistent.
q01_coarse_limits.walking_check: Normal walking on a 10 degree slope stays far inside: hip about -15 to +50, knee 0 to about 70, ankle about -20 to +20 degrees (typical gait ranges, not looked up in this session). Margins to the bounds are 35 degrees or more. The limits cannot fail ordinary strides and will only trip a gross scale, unit, wrap or sign-and-offset error.
q01_coarse_limits.L2_30deg_per_sample: Reasonable: a stride is 150 samples over 0.5-2.5 s, i.e. 3-17 ms per sample; 30 degrees per sample means about 1,800-9,000 degrees/s, versus real gait joint speeds of a few hundred degrees/s (a few degrees per sample). Catches 180/360 degree wraps and branch jumps, misses anything gradual. Edge: at the longest strides the threshold is higher in deg/s, still far above physiology.
edits: Label an ankle L1 pass 'not blatantly impossible, zero offset unreviewed', as drafted.
Move L3 to the structural layer (it cannot fail by construction under the 50-250 frame rule), as the draft already suggests.
State the source honestly as 'AAOS normal ranges as tabulated in a secondary source'.
Apply L1 and L2 only to channels with origin recorded in the T04 map (hook, copied, physics), after the v2 T04 outputs exist.
Keep the unchecked list (pelvis, segments, moments, powers, velocities); with D-UM21-Q01-1 = B no per-task ranges.
